info.title: zproject API
info.description:
Plans served by zprojectd on 127.0.0.1:8788, published on the tailnet by
`tailscale serve`. Every request except `GET /v1/health` needs
`Authorization: Bearer zpt_<id>.<secret>`. Each operation names the
scope it needs (`x-zproject-scope`; `any` = any valid token), whether
it is destructive (`x-zproject-destructive`; tokens with
`requireConfirm` must confirm it) and whether it takes `?dryRun=true`
(`x-zproject-dry-run`).

get.summary: Server health and versions (no token needed)

400.description: 400 bad_host: the Host header is not one of the configured names

post.summary: Create a project (tokens limited to named projects cannot)

200.description: The updated project, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true

delete.summary: Tombstone a project and its tasks (destructive)

200.description: The tombstoned project, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

get.summary: The task tree with WBS codes (1, 1.1, 1.2, 2, ...)
The project as a file (JSON, CSV, OpenDocument spreadsheet or MS Project XML)
get.description:
One project's live rows as a download (SPEC.md §7.9), with
`Content-Disposition: attachment` and a file name made from the
project's name.

- `json`: full fidelity, `{"format": "zproject-export",
  "schemaVersion": 1, project, tasks (with `wbs`), dependencies,
  calendars (with their exceptions)}`.
- `csv`: the task table, RFC 4180, UTF-8, CRLF, with a header row:
  WBS, Level, Title, Type (task, milestone or summary), Mode,
  Duration (days), Start, Finish, Predecessors (`3FS+2d`), %
  Complete, Status, Priority, Constraint, Constraint date,
  Deadline, Actual start, Actual finish, Fixed cost, Notes, ID.
  Text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage
  return gets a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't run it.
- `ods`: OpenDocument spreadsheet with Tasks (the CSV columns, as
  typed numbers, dates and percentages), Dependencies and Project
  sheets.
- `mspdi`: Microsoft Project XML (opens in MS Project, ProjectLibre
  and GanttProject): the outline, durations, dates, milestones,
  links with lag, constraints, deadlines, % complete, notes and
  the calendars used, with their holidays.

PDF and PNG need a renderer and are made by the desktop app.

get.summary: A project's tasks in WBS order, optionally filtered

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text to find in the title or notes (case-insensitive)

post.summary: Add a task to the project

patch.description: A summary task (one with live children) derives percentComplete, status, actualStart and actualFinish from its children (SPEC.md §5.3); changing any of them on a summary is a 400 validation error. A write to a child also updates its summaries, each with its own revision and change record; a dry run lists those updates too.

200.description: The updated task, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true

delete.summary: Tombstone a task and its subtree, with their links (destructive)

200.description: The tombstoned task, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

post.summary: Move a task to a new parent and/or position within its project (If-Match honoured)
post.description: Reparents and/or reorders a task and its subtree within the same project (SPEC.md §7.1). `position` is the 0-based index among the destination's live children, not counting the task itself; omitted, the task goes last. The destination's children are renumbered 1..n (`order`), each sibling whose order changes getting its own revision and change record, and the old and new parents' summaries are rolled up again (SPEC.md §5.3). Moving a task under itself or one of its descendants is a 409 cycle, as is a move that would loop through links (a task linked to the summary it moves under); a milestone, deleted or missing parent, a parent in another project or a position out of range is a 400. Moving to the place it already has changes nothing. If-Match is the moved task's rev.

200.description: The moved task, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true (op "move" for the task, "update" for renumbered siblings and summaries)

post.summary: Restore a deleted task and the subtree deleted with it (destructive)
post.description: Undoes a task delete: the task and those of its descendants that the same delete tombstoned come back with their old parent and order; descendants deleted earlier stay deleted. Summaries are rolled up again. 409 conflict if the task is not deleted, its project or parent is deleted (restore the parent first), or its parent has become a milestone. The links deleted with the tasks come back too, when both their tasks are live again and the pair hasn't been linked since; a restore that would close a loop with links made since is a 409 cycle. Destructive (SPEC.md §9.3): tokens with requireConfirm need the confirmId of a dry run. If-Match is the deleted task's rev. The body, if any, must be an empty object.

200.description: The restored task, or a dry-run result with a confirmId (op "restore" for restored tasks, "update" for summaries)

get.summary: The change records of one task, oldest first

post.description: Calendars are shared by every project, so writing one needs a token for all projects (403 forbidden_project otherwise). `base` must be a live calendar, with no loop of bases and at most 8 deep.

patch.description: Standard has no base. Needs a token for all projects.

200.description: The updated calendar, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true

delete.summary: Tombstone a calendar and its exceptions (destructive)
delete.description: 409 conflict with details.reason `standard` for Standard, or `in_use` with details.usedBy {projects, tasks, calendars} while a live project, task or calendar still uses it. Needs a token for all projects.

200.description: The tombstoned calendar, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

get.summary: A calendar's own exceptions, by date

post.summary: Add a holiday, a non-working stretch or custom hours
post.description: `holiday` and `non_working` take days out of the calendar; `custom_hours` changes the hours of days that are working anyway. One exception spans at most 366 days. Needs a token for all projects.

200.description: The tombstoned exception, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

post.summary: Add a year's public holidays (computed, not fetched)
post.description: Adds the year's US federal holidays (observed dates, so New Year's Day of the next year can fall on 31 December) that the calendar doesn't already have as a holiday that day; each is its own exception. The body, if any, must be empty. Needs a token for all projects.

200.description: The exceptions added, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Only the links into or out of this task

post.summary: Link two tasks of one project
post.description: Both tasks must be live and in the same project (400). A second live link between the same two tasks in the same direction is 409 `conflict` with details.reason `duplicate` and details.existing. A link that would close a loop, through other links or through the task tree (a task and its own summary), is 409 `cycle` with details.path, the task ids around the loop. Links don't move any dates until the scheduling engine is live on the server (plan S5).

patch.summary: Change a link's type or lag (If-Match honoured)
patch.description: Only `type` and `lag` change. A link's tasks are fixed: sending `predecessor`, `successor` or `project` is a 400; delete the link and add another instead.

200.description: The updated link, or a dry-run result with ?dryRun=true
The tombstoned link, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

get.summary: The sync feed (needs projects:read too, and access to every project)
Every token's metadata (never the secret or its hash)

post.summary: Create a device, app or agent token; the secret is returned once

201.description: Created; `token` is shown only in this response

delete.summary: Revoke a token; takes effect on its next request (destructive)

200.description: The revoked token, or a dry-run result with a confirmId

post.summary: Take a backup now (the same as the nightly timer)

200.description: The files written and the ones pruned

since.name: since
since.description: Return rows with seq greater than this

dryRun.name: dryRun
dryRun.description: Validate and describe the change without making it

ifMatch.name: If-Match
ifMatch.description: The rev the change is based on; 412 if it moved on

confirm.name: X-Zproject-Confirm
confirm.description: confirmId from a dry run of the identical request (single use, 5 minutes)

Validation.description: 400 validation: the request is malformed or a field is invalid

Unauthenticated.description: 401 unauthenticated: missing, unknown, expired or revoked token

RevMismatch.description: 412 rev_mismatch: If-Match did not match the current rev

calendar.description: A live calendar's id; null = Standard
A live calendar's id; null = the project's

percentComplete.description: Derived (duration-weighted over leaf tasks) on a summary task.

order.description: Position among the parent's children (1 = first; gaps are allowed). Read-only: a create or PATCH body with `order` is a 400 validation error; reorder with POST /v1/tasks/{id}/move.

parent.description: The new parent task (null = top level); omitted, the parent stays

position.description: 0-based index among the new parent's live children, not counting the task; omitted = last

hours.description: More than 0 on a working day; 0 otherwise

base.description: The calendar this one inherits from (its work week, if this has none, and its exceptions)

workWeek.description: Monday first, with at least one working day; null = the base's (at the root, Monday–Friday 8 h)

LinkType.description: FS: the successor starts after the predecessor finishes; SS: it starts no earlier than the predecessor starts; FF: it finishes no earlier than the predecessor finishes.

Lag.description: Whole working days of the successor's calendar; negative is a lead

project.description: Optional; must be the tasks' project

ripple.description: Schedule effects (empty until the scheduling engine lands)

confirmId.description: For destructive operations; send it in X-Zproject-Confirm

token.description: zpt_<id>.<secret>, shown once; store it in a keychain
